item.text: {"text":"HR@10 with 99 sampled negatives measures ranking within the sampled candidate set; it can reverse model ordering relative to full-catalog evaluation. Keep the pinned users, candidates and evaluator unchanged, and limit conclusions to this benchmark. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish this inconsistency. Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can also overfit a noisy validation criterion, making the winning validation score optimistic ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and the four-category macro-average by 0.00125.\n\nA suitable comparison protocol: retain per-user hit indicators; bootstrap users within each category, using identical resampled indices for baseline and challenger; recompute the macro-average difference and report its 95% interval. This adapts [paired bootstrap resampling](https://people.csail.mit.edu/koehn/publications/bootstrap2004.pdf). Such intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models; they do not capture training-seed variation or remove adaptive-selection bias. Within 43,200 GPU-seconds, predeclare a small GRU4Rec ablation set covering loss, negative sampling, hidden size and dropout; prioritize loss/sampling because [GRU4Rec research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847) identifies these as consequential. Keep seed 42, the 200-epoch ceiling and 200 batches/epoch; record every trial’s compute, including failures. Use four slots for independent trials, retain one model/category, and reserve held-out evaluation for the final selected configuration."}
